props.title: Your course updates itself when your sources change
props.intro: Edit a doc or merge to a repo. ulams finds every lesson and question that cites it and proposes the update. You approve, and learners keep their progress.
props.valueLine: Courses stop going stale, and nothing changes without your approval.
props.description: An animated example in three steps. First, a line in docs/slo.md changes from 99.9 % to 99.95 % and a new line about the 30-day budget is added. Second, ulams finds the lesson paragraph and the quiz question that cite docs/slo.md section 2. Third, a proposal with a red and green diff appears, the author clicks Approve, the lesson text updates and a badge confirms that learner progress was kept.

props.title: Build a course from a document in minutes
props.intro: Drop in a runbook, answer three questions, and review a cited outline and drafts before anything goes live.
props.valueLine: From a PDF to a published, cited course, with you approving every step.
props.description: An animated example of the studio course builder. A file named incident-runbook.pdf is dropped in, three interview answers appear (engineers, 45 minutes, a quiz per lesson), an outline of three modules and five lessons grows with a source chip on each lesson, one lesson streams in with citations, a quiz question cites its source, an example cost counter reaches 18 cents, and Apply publishes the course.

lesson.title: Severity levels
lesson.text: Sev 1 means customers cannot check out. Page the on-call lead and open an incident channel straight away.

props.title: Manage your academy from Claude, Claude Code or your terminal
props.intro: Use Claude Code, Claude or any MCP-compatible agent, the command line or the API. The studio is one way to run ulams, not the only one.
props.valueLine: One platform, every interface your team already works in.
props.legal: Claude and Claude Code are products of Anthropic. ulams is independent and not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.

props.title: Your brand, your academy, one course per source
props.intro: Bring your style and your content. ulams gives you a branded academy on its own subdomain, a separate cited course for every source, and the learner analytics for each of them.
props.valueLine: Your look, your subdomain, your content, and clear numbers per course.
props.description: An animated example in four steps. One: an agent such as Claude Code, with the ulams CLI and the Figma or Stitch MCP attached, reads a design (a Figma file, a Stitch DESIGN.md, a brand guide PDF or a logo and colours), extracts colours, fonts, logo and corner radius, and runs ulams theme set and ulams settings set; a custom front built on the headless API is shown as the alternative. Two: a themed academy appears on its own subdomain, acme.ulams.app, with a landing page, a course catalogue and an admin, all in the extracted brand. Three: documents, PDFs, a Git repository and a web page each become their own cited course, built by the course builder and kept in sync by Living Course. Four: a per-course dashboard shows learner progress, quiz performance, learners at risk and the sections that confuse people. All names and values are an example.

props.title: An LMS that earns trust
props.intro: Built for developer and customer education: content that changes with every release, sold and delivered to many audiences.

items.title: Living Course
items.text: Courses stay in sync with the docs and repos they come from, and adapt to each learner.

items.title: Cited by design
items.text: Every AI-generated element cites the source fragment it is based on. AI proposes, the author approves the diff.

items.title: A site per customer
items.text: Each tenant gets its own subdomain, theme and isolated database: white-label academies for customers and partners.

items.title: Self-hosted, open core
items.text: MIT-licensed core you can run on your own servers. Your content and learner data stay yours; no lock-in.

items.title: Standards first
items.text: H5P, SCORM, cmi5, xAPI and LTI 1.3 work today; the same course can be delivered anywhere.

items.title: Commerce built in
items.text: Catalogue, checkout and subscriptions through a headless Sylius shop; access granted only from verified orders.

props.title: How a course keeps up with its sources
props.intro: The killer feature on our roadmap: when your docs change, the course proposes its own update, and you stay in control.

items.title: Connect sources
items.text: Point ulams at docs, repos and release notes. They become the only ground truth for the course.

items.title: Generate with citations
items.text: Lessons, quizzes and interactives are drafted from approved objectives, each element linked to its source fragment.

items.title: Review diffs when sources change
items.text: A change upstream becomes an update proposal: a reviewable diff you approve, edit or reject.

final.intro: The killer feature: when your docs change, the course proposes its own update, and you stay in control.

props.title: Six academies, one platform
props.intro: Each demo is a separate tenant with its own theme, course and data, running on the same ulams install. Open it as a learner or step into its admin.
props.note: Demos reset every hour. No sign-up: you are logged in automatically.

props.title: Delivered anywhere
props.intro: Standards over lock-in: bring existing packages, track learning anywhere, integrate through the API.

props.title: Every feature, from video to analytics
props.intro: The full list, grouped and collapsed. Every line links to the package or the guide behind it.

groups.title: Lessons and content types
groups.summary: Mix the content types below freely inside one course.

items.title: Seven built-in topic types
items.text: Video, audio, image, PDF, rich text (Markdown), oEmbed and H5P topics in one course.

items.title: LiaScript courses
items.text: Write a course as LiaScript Markdown. Every change, upload or restore adds an immutable version, so nothing is overwritten.

items.title: Interactive web apps
items.text: Upload a zip with an index.html and a manifest. It plays in a sandbox on the tenant content origin, with a content security policy per version and versions you can pin or follow.

items.title: Layout lessons
items.text: A lesson body assembled from approved learning components such as timelines, flip cards, steps and callouts.

items.title: Student projects
items.text: Learners upload their solutions as files.

items.title: Courses, categories and tags
items.text: Organise the catalogue with categories and tags.

items.title: Dictionaries and pages
items.text: Manage dictionaries with their expressions and publish static pages.

items.title: Bookmarks and notes
items.text: Learners keep bookmarks and notes in one data model.

groups.title: Learner experience
groups.summary: A server-rendered learner app with a course player that works on small screens.

items.title: Course player
items.text: A program tree with the status of every topic (done, current, open or locked), a progress bar and a finish page, with a player for each topic type.

items.title: Notes and bookmarks
items.text: Learners save notes and bookmarks while they learn.

items.title: Accessible by default
items.text: WCAG 2.2 AA is the quality bar for learner-facing pages, scanned with axe in the tests.

items.title: Sign in through a browser
items.text: Learners and tutors sign in on the web app, and the same session approves CLI and agent tokens.

groups.title: Media pipeline
groups.summary: Upload once; the platform converts, resizes and guards the files.

items.title: Video to adaptive HLS with ffmpeg
items.text: A queued ffmpeg job converts every uploaded video into an HLS stream with several bitrates (250, 500 and 1000 kbps by default, resolution configurable). Processing can be switched off and the storage disk chosen.

items.title: On-demand image resizing
items.text: Request any width and height, or a named size such as thumbnail, and get a cached, optimised copy: one call that redirects, or a JSON batch for many images. Size limits and rate limits protect the server.

items.title: Safe uploads
items.text: One guard for every upload: size, extension, MIME type sniffed from the content, virus scan, and zip-slip, symlink and zip-bomb checks for archives.

items.title: Media library
items.text: Admins list, find, upload, move and delete files in the media library.

groups.title: Quizzes and assessment
groups.summary: Knowledge tests, feedback forms and tasks.

items.title: GIFT quizzes
items.text: Eight question types: multiple choice, multiple choice with several right answers, true/false, short answers, matching, numerical, essay and description.

items.title: Attempts, timers and shuffling
items.text: Limit attempts and the time per attempt, randomise the order of questions and answers per attempt (stable on refresh), and let teachers grade essays by hand.

items.title: Questionnaires
items.text: Create questionnaires to collect learners’ answers.

items.title: Tasks
items.text: Users create their own tasks or assign tasks to other users.

items.title: Certificates
items.text: A PDF certificate is issued when a learner finishes a course, from a template designed in the admin panel (the default is A4 landscape with a QR code). The template is stored with each certificate.

groups.title: H5P interactive content
groups.summary: H5P runs in its own isolated service, so its GPL code never mixes with the MIT core. These are the content types published on h5p.org.

items.title: Isolated H5P service
items.text: Create, edit and play H5P content inside lessons, served by Lumi’s h5p-nodejs-library in a separate service.

items.title: Install from the H5P Hub
items.text: Platform administrators install, restrict and remove content types. Libraries are shared by all academies while content and results stay per tenant.

groups.title: Standards and interoperability
groups.summary: Bring existing packages, track learning anywhere, move courses between systems.

items.title: SCORM 1.2 and 2004
items.text: Upload SCORM packages, play them in lessons and track each learner’s progress per SCO.

items.title: cmi5 and xAPI
items.text: Launch cmi5 assignable units; a first-party xAPI learning record store receives the statements.

items.title: LTI 1.3, both directions
items.text: Launch external tools inside lessons with grade passback, or let Moodle, Canvas and other LMSs launch ulams courses.

items.title: Course import and export
items.text: Move courses between installations as .ulam packages with a content.json and all assets.

items.title: CSV users
items.text: Export and import users as CSV.

items.title: Adapt Learning
items.text: Adapt course sources as versioned JSON, built into SCORM by an isolated GPL-3.0 worker. Off by default.

groups.title: AI and Living Course
groups.summary: AI proposes, the author approves: every change is a reviewable diff and every generated element cites its source.

items.title: AI Course Builder
items.text: Turn Markdown, PDF or DOCX into a cited course: a short interview, an outline with learning objectives you approve, generated lessons and quizzes, applied through the LMS domain services.

items.title: Living Course
items.text: Watches the sources of a course, finds the lessons and quiz questions that cite changed passages and proposes cited updates for you to review as one diff. Learner progress is preserved by explicit rules.

items.title: Provider-agnostic LLM layer
items.text: One access layer to large language models for every package, with an Anthropic driver and fake and disabled drivers for tests.

items.title: Course statistics
items.text: Average time and time per topic, people who bought, started and finished, finished topics and an attendance list, exportable to a spreadsheet.

items.title: Topic and quiz statistics
items.text: Average time per topic and a summary of the quiz results for each GIFT quiz.

items.title: Quiz reports and manual grading
items.text: Every attempt filtered by date, course and student, with each answer visible. Grade essays or correct any automatic score and the total updates.

items.title: Dashboard charts
items.text: Money spent per course, course popularity, time spent per course and tutor popularity, plus best-rated courses and variants that show tutors only their own courses.

items.title: Activity over a period
items.text: New users, active users, and courses started and finished between any two dates.

items.title: Metric history
items.text: Metrics can be snapshotted on a schedule, so the API returns a value for a past date. Off in the default configuration.

items.title: Questionnaires
items.text: Surveys with rating, text and review questions, optional maximum scores, public or hidden answers and results per questionnaire.

items.title: xAPI statements
items.text: cmi5 results land in the built-in learning record store, with a statement list in the admin panel.

items.title: SCORM tracking
items.text: Progress per learner and per SCO, stored for each SCORM package.

items.title: Notification log
items.text: Who was notified of what and when, filtered by user, event and date.

items.title: Update audit trail
items.text: Every Living Course decision lands in a tamper-evident audit trail, and learner progress follows explicit rules.

items.title: Per-course author analytics
items.text: A dashboard per course with progress, completion, quiz performance and the sections that confuse people.

items.title: At-risk learners
items.text: Rule-based risk scoring with human-readable reasons and per-tenant thresholds, and rate-limited nudges.

items.title: AI tutor
items.text: Answers only from the course sources with citations, and says when a question is out of scope.

groups.title: Analytics for sales
groups.summary: Revenue, customers and orders, from the same data the shop runs on.

items.title: Revenue per course
items.text: The sum of paid order items for each course, as a dashboard chart and an API metric.

items.title: Top-selling and best-rated courses
items.text: Rank courses by sales and by rating.

items.title: New and returning customers
items.text: Cart statistics show new customers, returning customers and spend per customer.

items.title: From purchase to completion
items.text: For each course, how many people bought it, started it and finished it.

items.title: Orders
items.text: Subtotal, tax, total, items, buyer and status for every order, filtered by date range, user, product and status.

items.title: Payments
items.text: Amount, currency, status and the paid-for object of every payment: new, redirect, paid, failed, cancelled or refunded.

items.title: Spreadsheet exports
items.text: Course and topic statistics export to a spreadsheet for your own analysis.

groups.title: Live learning
groups.summary: Webinars, meetings, in-person events and one-to-one sessions.

items.title: Webinars with YouTube livestreams
items.text: Schedule webinars with reminders one hour and one day before, and stream them live to YouTube.

items.title: Jitsi meetings
items.text: Generate the parameters of the Jitsi player for video meetings.

items.title: Pencil Spaces
items.text: Integration with Pencil Spaces.

items.title: Stationary events
items.text: Manage in-person events.

items.title: Consultations
items.text: One-to-one conversations, with enquiries for free consultation access that users with the right permission can accept.

items.title: Mattermost
items.text: Integration with Mattermost.

groups.title: Commerce and access
groups.summary: The LMS owns entitlements; access is granted only from verified orders.

items.title: Shopping cart
items.text: A cart with buyable products.

items.title: Products and subscriptions
items.text: Sell single products, bundles and subscriptions (with a period, auto-renew and an optional trial), with a price, old price, tax rate, extra fees and per-user and total purchase limits.

items.title: Voucher rules
items.text: Fixed or percentage discounts on the whole cart or on chosen products, with an active window, total and per-user limits, minimum and maximum cart value, and product, category or user restrictions.

items.title: Verified payment callbacks
items.text: Stripe callbacks are accepted only with a valid signature or after the PaymentIntent is fetched from Stripe, 3-D Secure included. Free orders use a gateway that refuses any non-zero amount.

items.title: Mobile in-app purchases
items.text: A RevenueCat gateway accepts purchases only when a server-side receipt verifier is configured.

items.title: Publishing and access
items.text: Draft, published, scheduled and archived courses; public courses and free preview topics; access for users and groups, access requests and invitations by e-mail.

items.title: Stripe and Przelewy24
items.text: Take payments through Stripe or Przelewy24; gateway keys can be changed in the settings.

items.title: Vouchers
items.text: Coupons that discount a cart before the order is placed.

items.title: Invoices
items.text: Generate a PDF invoice from an order.

items.title: Course access
items.text: Grant access to a course to individual users and groups, or assign users who do not have an account yet.

items.title: Headless Sylius shop
items.text: A separate Sylius 2.x service behind one frontend: catalogue, cart and checkout there, entitlements in the LMS.

groups.title: Platform and administration
groups.summary: One deployment, many academies, every setting in the admin panel.

items.title: A site per customer
items.text: Each tenant gets its own host, database, storage bucket, keys and Redis prefix, so a token from one tenant is rejected by every other.

items.title: Public demos
items.text: Visitors log in as a student, tutor or admin without a password; the demo resets every hour.

items.title: Users, groups and permissions
items.text: User, group and profile management with roles and permissions behind a REST API.

items.title: Settings and custom fields
items.text: Change configuration from the admin panel and add unlimited extra primitive fields to any model.

items.title: Translations
items.text: Manage translations.

items.title: Email, SMS and PDF templates
items.text: Editable templates for email, SMS (through Twilio) and PDF, bound to events.

items.title: Notifications
items.text: Log and broadcast notifications from every package, register device tokens for bulk notifications and sync with MailerLite.

items.title: Reports
items.text: Statistics and reports.

items.title: User import and invitations
items.text: Import and export users as CSV or Excel, and invite people who do not have an account yet.

items.title: White-label themes
items.text: Each academy has its own theme preset and accent colour, with accessible contrast checked on the server.

items.title: In-app notifications and push
items.text: Every package event can be stored as an in-app notification, and administrators send push messages to mobile devices.

groups.title: Security and operations
groups.summary: Run it yourself, on a shared host or a cluster, with isolation between academies.

items.title: Sandboxed content
items.text: H5P runs in its own service and interactive apps in an opaque sandbox on a separate content origin, with a content security policy per version.

items.title: Security headers and CSP reports
items.text: A Content Security Policy for the learner front, the admin and the API, with violation reports; start in report-only mode, then enforce.

items.title: Rate limits
items.text: Throttles on device login, tokens, the platform API, per-token limits, webhooks and public endpoints, tunable by environment variables.

items.title: Self-hosting options
items.text: Docker Compose, a shared MyDevil account, or a VPS behind Cloudflare, each with a written guide.

items.title: High availability
items.text: A reference topology that separates the stateless components from the ones that hold state, zero-downtime deploys and migrations, and Kubernetes notes.

items.title: Backups and restores
items.text: Back up a whole installation and restore either all of it or a single tenant.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text: Health checks for every container, HTTP endpoints to probe, worker and scheduler checks, logs and error tracking.

items.title: Licences kept apart
items.text: An MIT core, with GPL components such as H5P and Adapt isolated in their own services, and a page listing the licences of every image.

groups.title: For developers
groups.summary: Headless by design: everything the apps do goes through the same API.

items.title: Extensible by packages
items.text: Every feature is a composer package with its own routes, permissions, settings and events. A worked example shows the pattern end to end.

items.title: MCP server for AI agents
items.text: ulams mcp serves every CLI command as MCP tools over stdio or Streamable HTTP, for Claude Code, Claude Desktop and other MCP clients: 23 tools by default, up to 535 with all toolsets. Built from the repository today; the npm package is planned.

items.title: Safe by default for agents
items.text: Read-only mode, a switch that hides destructive tools, dry-run plans with a diff for every write, and single-use confirmation tokens for deletes. The API still enforces the user’s permissions and the token’s scopes.

items.title: Agent audit log
items.text: Scoped tokens record what an agent did, with the client and the agent name sent on every request.

items.title: Build courses from the command line
items.text: The Course Builder and Living Course are commands and MCP tools: start a run, answer the interview, approve the outline, apply, and poll long runs with a wait handle.

items.title: Machine-readable CLI
items.text: Every command returns a JSON envelope with exit codes, describes itself with ulams schema, and logs in through the browser with a device code. Shell completion included.

items.title: Pages as data
items.text: Landing and course pages are JSON documents of catalogue components, rendered on the server and generated by the Course Builder, so a model never writes page code.

items.title: OpenAPI reference
items.text: Every endpoint is documented in OpenAPI, with a searchable API browser and Swagger UI on every API host.

items.title: TypeScript SDK
items.text: Typed requests for servers and browsers, with pagination, error handling and idempotent writes.

items.title: Scoped API tokens
items.text: Tokens limited to the scopes you choose, with an audit log, Idempotency-Key and X-Request-Id.

items.title: Command line
items.text: The ulams CLI calls any API endpoint from scripts and agents, with JSON output and exit codes.

items.title: Inbound webhooks
items.text: Webhooks for Living Course Git pushes, Stripe and Jitsi recordings. There are no outgoing webhooks yet.

props.title: How ulams compares
props.intro: ulams is built for developers and AI agents first: courses are managed through the REST API and the TypeScript SDK, with an agent-first CLI and MCP server coming. Compared with open-source and creator platforms, and with enterprise suites; our roadmap items are marked Coming.
